scope: Development study on one H100 node: complete solves of the 2D Kovasznay objective with larger interior point sets, where the gradient is a larger share of each evaluation than at the frozen 2,048 points. Each point count is a new problem instance (different collocation points, same network, optimizer program, validation sets and acceptance), not the frozen problem at scale. No H100 ratio is pooled with or compared against the H20 campaign.
motivation: The registered 2D ablation found that at 2,048 points native GL8 (cell C) computes the full gradient 1.71 times faster than compiled Q10 (cell A), but optimization alone is no faster (0.95), because the L-BFGS phase costs about 6.5 ms per evaluation in every cell (post hoc), against 0.17-0.28 ms of gradient replay.

source.unchanged: bench_gpu.py, gpu_engine.py, problem.py, solve.py and every flashns module

optimizer: unchanged solve.py program: 4,000 Adam updates, strong-Wolfe L-BFGS in blocks of at most 20 iterations / 25 evaluations, history 50, stop checks before training, every 100 Adam updates and after every block, 500-block extension as in bench_gpu.complete_solve
acceptance: unchanged: all six metrics on the fixed 8,192-point validation set and the independent scalar-AD set; a non-converged solve is a failed solve

per_size_and_pair: paired geometric mean of setup plus optimization seconds
paired geometric mean of optimization-only seconds
paired geometric mean of optimization seconds per evaluation
number of jointly accepted pairs and how many favour the second cell in optimization time

decision_rule.solve_level_gain: at a size, C has a solve-level gain over A if the optimization-only geometric mean of A/C exceeds 1.03 and at least 5 of 6 jointly accepted pairs have C faster in optimization; same rule for B over A and C over B
decision_rule.otherwise: no solve-level gain at that size (reported with the statistics); fewer than 5 jointly accepted pairs is reported as not decidable

predictions.note: expectations, not gates: optimization time ~ 4,000 x (replay + 0.1 ms) + L-BFGS evaluations x (replay + 6.3 ms), with the ablation replay medians and similar evaluation counts

phase_split: descriptive: Adam-phase and L-BFGS-phase optimization milliseconds per evaluation from each solve's progress rows

execution.allocation: one ACC node, four H100 lanes, 3 h, run once; cluster-side driver with embedded start command; tasks in size order (16,384 first), shuffled within a size
execution.reason: 36 solves; worst case about 250 s each at 65,536 points
